subject: maths
question: If sinθ = 5/13, and θ is acute, find the value of (1 + cot²θ).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use identity: 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ

sinθ = 5/13

⇒ cosecθ = 13/5

⇒ cosec²θ = (13/5)² = 169/25

**∴ The correct answer is 169/25 value.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

⇒ sinθ = 5/13

Formula used:

⇒ 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ

⇒ cosecθ = 1 ÷ sinθ

Calculation:

⇒ cosecθ = 1 ÷ (5/13)

⇒ cosecθ = 13/5

⇒ cosec²θ = (13/5)²

⇒ cosec²θ = 169/25

⇒ 1 + cot²θ = 169/25

**∴ The correct answer is 169/25 value.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identity

1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ is a standard trigonometric identity.

Reciprocal Ratios

cosecθ = 1 ÷ sinθ and secθ = 1 ÷ cosθ.

Acute Angle Property

For acute angles, all trigonometric ratios are positive.

Common Right Triangle

If sinθ = 5/13, then the corresponding right triangle sides are 5, 12 and 13.
